evidence_scope: All declarations inventoried; 549 effective setters receive defaults/wrong-type/declared-type sweeps. Family scenarios are representative, not one proof per invariant or every association/mutation sequence.
supplemental_helper_scope: Internal dependency queries, not additional normative 2.4.1 operation declarations.
limitations: Registration and declaration audits are not UML conformance certification.
Generic supplemental normative prose remains unsupported (UML2.4.1.prose); execution traces, PackageMerge reconciliation and behavioral protocol-conformance proof are not supplied.
Opaque expression evaluation, foreign lexical default representations and domain collection types require explicit adapters/facts.
Activity autonomy, relative TimeEvent starting times, conditional trigger assignment and transformation Behavior purity require trusted facts when the model cannot establish them.
Core XMI 2.4.1 exchange is implemented in 0.18.0 (XMI241_SUPPORT.md); runtime profile applications, CMOF/vendor adapters and migration remain separate unsupported contracts.
Implicit region/machine extension preserves original structure by reference; it does not clone inherited composite members into the extension.
Connector feature compatibility is the documented nominal/signature interpretation; trace conformance and arbitrary execution are not proved.

shared_reference_caveats.PackageMerge: The model represents receiving/merged Package links. The normative reconciliation/merge algorithm is not implemented.
shared_reference_caveats.ProfileApplication-isStrict: Strict availability views and checked creation support UML metaclass references, imported profiles, extended subtypes and conflicting filters. Direct constructors remain available for general model editing. Non-UML metaclasses need an adapter; UI presentation and CMOF interoperability remain open.
shared_reference_caveats.Stereotype: Runtime typed tags support effective inherited/redefined properties, literal defaults, bounds, readonly values, enumerations, profile Class/DataType objects, binary navigable inverses, composition and deletion. Model-defined primitive lexical values retain exact type identity; Python semantics require explicit per-definition codecs. User constraints use trusted Python callbacks or Boolean literals, never arbitrary OCL execution. Derived/general default evaluators, association-owned runtime navigation, full CMOF serialization and exhaustive profile semantics remain open.
shared_reference_caveats.ProtocolConformance: Specific/general machine links are represented. Behavioral protocol-conformance proof is not implemented.
shared_reference_caveats.Continuation-same_name: Peer traversal uses context-owned Interactions and role identity with literal selector kind/value. A complete census of every Interaction sharing context and arbitrary domain selector equivalence remains open.
shared_reference_caveats.Message-signature_is_operation_reply: The XMI predicate is preserved, including vacuous direct values. validate() additionally enforces prose:Message.reply_argument_types on direct typed values, first expression operands and wildcards; arbitrary expression evaluation remains outside this check.
shared_reference_caveats.Message-sending_receiving_message_event: The check uses represented ordered fragment containment with nested fragments visited before following siblings. A full partial-order semantics for parallel/alternative operands and GeneralOrdering is not implemented.
shared_reference_caveats.InteractionConstraint-dynamic_variables: Trusted reference facts are checked against represented covered lifeline roles/types, interaction parameters/context attributes and read-only Properties. Full runtime ownership/global/write-once semantics remains a project approximation.
shared_reference_caveats.InteractionConstraint-global_data: Trusted reference facts and represented read-only Properties are supported. Arbitrary domain global/write-once storage semantics is not represented by core UML and is not proved.
shared_reference_caveats.InteractionOperand-guard_contain_referen: Trusted guard reference facts are checked against represented operand coverage/context. General domain-global and write-once facts remain incomplete.
shared_reference_caveats.InteractionOperand-guard_directly_prior: Guard composite ownership is checked. Graphical placement immediately above a fragment requires UMLDI/layout semantics and is not proved.
shared_reference_caveats.ObjectNode-input_output_parameter: Input/output counts, multiplicities and nominal type variance are checked (with a documented source-body correction). Absence of side effects of the selection Behavior is not proved.
shared_reference_caveats.ObjectFlow-input_and_output_parameter: The XMI count/bounds predicate is preserved. validate() additionally enforces selection input/output types through prose:ObjectFlow.selection_types. Behavior purity remains an external evidence obligation.
shared_reference_caveats.ObjectFlow-transformation_behavior: The XMI count predicate is preserved. validate() additionally enforces upstream/input and output/downstream conformance through prose:ObjectFlow.transformation_types. Behavior purity remains an external evidence obligation.
shared_reference_caveats.DecisionNode-two_input_parameters: The XMI count predicate is preserved. validate() additionally enforces ordered regular/decision-flow input types through prose:DecisionNode.input_types; unrepresented token types remain unsupported.
shared_reference_caveats.DecisionNode-incoming_control_one_input_: The XMI count predicate is preserved. validate() additionally enforces decisionInputFlow token-type conformance through prose:DecisionNode.input_types; unrepresented types remain unsupported.
shared_reference_caveats.DecisionNode-incoming_object_one_input_p: The XMI count predicate is preserved. validate() additionally enforces the sole object input type through prose:DecisionNode.input_types; unrepresented types remain unsupported.

source_description: The query allFeatures() gives all of the features in the namespace of the classifier. In general, through mechanisms such as inheritance, this will be a larger set than feature.
The query allParents() gives all of the direct and indirect ancestors of a generalized Classifier.
The query conformsTo() gives true for a classifier that defines a type that conforms to another. This is used, for example, in the specification of signature conformance for operations.
The general classifiers are the classifiers referenced by the generalization relationships.
The query hasVisibilityOf() determines whether a named element is visible in the classifier. By default all are visible. It is only called when the argument is something owned by a parent.

The query inherit() defines how to inherit a set of elements. Here the operation is defined to inherit them all. It is intended to be redefined in circumstances where inheritance is affected by redefinition.
The inherit operation is overridden to exclude redefined properties.
The query inheritableMembers() gives all of the members of a classifier that may be inherited in one of its descendants, subject to whatever visibility restrictions apply.
The inheritedMember association is derived by inheriting the inheritable members of the parents.
The inheritedMember association is derived by inheriting the inheritable members of the parents.
The query isTemplate() returns whether this templateable element is actually a template.

The query maySpecializeType() determines whether this classifier may have a generalization relationship to classifiers of the specified type. By default a classifier may specialize classifiers of the same or a more general type. It is intended to be redefined by classifiers that have different specialization constraints.
The query parents() gives all of the immediate ancestors of a generalized Classifier.

The Classifier that maps to a GeneralizationSet may neither be a specific nor a general Classifier in any of the Generalization relationships defined for that GeneralizationSet. In other words, a power type may not be an instance of itself nor may its instances also be its subclasses.
